result: The authors developed and validated a pan-neuronal antibody (PNab) that stains all nerve cells in Hydra. Validation included testing against three transgenic lines expressing fluorescent markers in neurons, with 100% co-localization (684/684, 149/149, and 51/51 cells), and confirmation that the ratio of nerve to epithelial cells (0.12) matched between PNab staining and traditional maceration methods.
evaluation: All three reviewers explicitly acknowledge PNab as a novel and useful tool. Reviewer 1 states the authors 'present outstanding imaging data with convincing evidence,' Reviewer 2 describes it as 'a novel PNab antibody' that 'may be used to detect the entire nervous system,' and Reviewer 3 notes 'the antibody can be used to visualize and study the nerve net under a variety of conditions.' The quantitative validation data is not questioned.

result: The authors demonstrate that Hydra has two separate nerve nets—one in the ectoderm and one in the endoderm—that do not contact each other. This was shown through systematic confocal imaging of complete tissue rings from four animals containing 133 nerve cells, with no connections observed between the two layers.
evaluation: All reviewers explicitly identify this as a major finding. Reviewer 1 states the work shows 'nerve cells in Hydra are organized as two separate nerve nets,' Reviewer 2 lists as a major observation that 'Nerve cells in the ectoderm and in the endoderm are organized in two separate nerve nets, which do not interact,' and Reviewer 3 notes 'the endodermal and ectodermal nerve net do not make any contacts through the mesoglea, in contrast to earlier assumptions.' No concerns are raised about this conclusion.

result: The nerve nets consist of discrete bundles of overlapping neurites running parallel to each other. In the ectoderm, ~80% of nerve tracks occur as bundles (often 3-5 neurites), while in the endoderm ~50% are single neurites and 50% are bundles of two neurites, with no larger bundles observed.
evaluation: All three reviewers explicitly recognize this as a major finding. Reviewer 1 notes 'TEM and block face SEM demonstrate that the two nerve nets consist of discrete bundles,' Reviewer 2 states 'Both nerve nets are composed of bundles of overlapping nerve processes' as one of three major observations, and Reviewer 3 describes how 'neurites align in parallel forming bundles of neurites over longer stretches, in particular in the ectoderm.' The quantitative data from TEM is not questioned.

result: There is a complete absence of nerve cells in the endoderm of tentacles, confirmed by PNab staining and consistent with historical observations by Hadži (1909).
evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly lists this as one of three major observations: 'the unexpected absence of nerve cells in the endoderm of the tentacles.' Reviewer 3 states 'they show that tentacle endoderm surprisingly does not have any neurons.' The finding is described as 'unexpected' but the data supporting it is not questioned by any reviewer.

result: The ectodermal nerve net is more directly associated with muscle processes and exhibits higher connectivity than the endodermal nerve net, as demonstrated by TEM and confocal imaging comparing the two layers.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 explicitly notes 'They show that ectodermal neurons make close contacts to the myoepithelial muscles, in contrast to the endodermal muscles.' This differential association is presented as a clear finding and is not questioned by any reviewer. The structural data supporting higher connectivity in the ectoderm (bundle complexity) is accepted.

result: The bundled organization of neurites supports a model for continuous nerve net growth by lateral addition of new nerve cells. This was confirmed by tracking newly differentiated nerve cells over 3 days, showing that most cells without neurites on day 1 were not associated with the nerve net, but by days 2-3 most extended neurites along existing nerve tracks.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 explicitly recognizes this contribution: 'the neurites align in parallel forming bundles of neurites over longer stretches...which offers a mechanism how new neurons are added laterally to the existing nerve net. This has important implications about the way the neurons might communicate with each other.' The tracking data and model are not questioned by any reviewer.

result: The spatial distribution of nerve cells varies dramatically along the body axis. The endoderm has very few nerve cells in the basal disk but relatively constant density (0.10-0.19) in the body column. The ectoderm has constant density (0.15-0.22) in the gastric region and peduncle but sharply increased numbers in the hypostome, tentacles, and basal disk.
evaluation: This quantitative characterization of nerve cell distribution is presented with data in Figure 6. While not explicitly highlighted by reviewers as a major finding, it is part of the comprehensive anatomical description that Reviewer 1 describes as 'outstanding imaging data with convincing evidence' and Reviewer 2 calls 'a comprehensive overview of the entire nervous system's spatial organization.' No concerns are raised about these measurements.

result: Different neural circuits express distinct innexins: CB circuit neurons (ec1/ec5) express innexin 2, RP1 circuit neurons (ec3) express innexins 6 and 14, and RP2 circuit neurons (en1) express innexin 2. This indicates that circuit-specific gap junctions can provide specificity for neural communication.
evaluation: This finding integrates scRNAseq data with the anatomical observations. While not explicitly discussed by reviewers, it is part of the comprehensive characterization that reviewers praise. Reviewer 2 notes the study aims 'to infer communication between cells,' and this innexin data directly addresses that goal. The data is presented clearly in Figure 12C and is not questioned.

result: Although PNab was raised against a peptide in H. vulgaris cadherin, it does not recognize cadherin protein. The peptide sequence is not conserved in H. oligactis and H. viridissima, yet PNab stains neurons in all three species. The identity of the actual PNab antigen is unknown, but PNab remains a highly specific pan-neuronal marker.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 explicitly notes 'the specificity of the antibody was not investigated' and states 'This antibody unexpectedly recognizes presumably all neurons in the Hydra polyp but the specificity of the antibody was not investigated.' While the reviewer acknowledges 'Regardless, the antibody can be used to visualize and study the nerve net,' the unknown identity of the antigen and lack of specificity investigation represents an acknowledged limitation.

result: Nerve cell bodies are roughly 10 μm long, with variable spacing between cell bodies (usually 50-100 μm) in both ectoderm and endoderm, as measured from confocal images and 3D reconstructions.
evaluation: These morphometric measurements are part of the detailed anatomical characterization. Reviewer 1 describes 'outstanding imaging data' and Reviewer 2 notes the study provides 'a comprehensive overview of the entire nervous system's spatial organization.' These specific measurements are not questioned and are consistent with the high-quality imaging praised by all reviewers.

result: Sensory cells constitute >50% of all endodermal nerve cells and are oriented toward the gastric cavity with sensory cilia extending into the cavity to monitor digestive activity and possibly osmotic strength.
evaluation: This observation about the high proportion of sensory cells in the endoderm is part of the comprehensive anatomical description. The functional speculation about monitoring digestion and osmotic strength is presented cautiously ('perhaps also'). Reviewers do not question this characterization, and it fits within the 'meticulous study' and 'stunning imaging results' praised by Reviewer 2.
